limitations: Normal `curl` protocol-level replay remains enabled. Eight logical transfers is not a wire-attempt bound. Nonzero reported retry counts, unexpected connection counts or missing required identity make a transfer unmatched; replay not reflected in those observations remains possible.
TCP receiver counters describe the guest receiver. They cannot locate incoming loss or expose the remote sender congestion window. Zero duplicate ACKs does not exclude a lost tail or whole flight.
The reassembly queue value is a sequence-space span. Advertised receive windows are already bytes. RTT is a local-sender measurement and can remain stale during downloads.
HTTP/2 event timestamps are client callback observations, not wire arrival times. A sent `WINDOW_UPDATE` callback does not establish peer receipt.
The printed stream window pair is effective received bytes and effective local window, not exact remaining stream credit in every state. Preserve both raw values.
Counter sampling, pipe draining and body-file polling can perturb transfers. Actual coverage, queue limits and reader read-completion gaps are retained; incomplete telemetry is not a zero finding.
Paired processes do not guarantee overlapping response-body intervals. Separate TCP flows can differ even on the same address and runner.
A batch without a slow H2 control does not demonstrate that H1 fixes the symptom. Stop after the scheduled batch without reruns.

analysis_guidance.counter_baselines: Use the first fully live valid category sample within each `observed_generation` as its own baseline. Start a new baseline after disappearance/reappearance or `collection_continuity_changed`; never bridge generations or use incomplete spans as zero deltas.
analysis_guidance.connection_identity: Process handle/PID/creation time remain tied to the owned child. Observed generations reflect sampled connection presence; a same-tuple reconnection entirely between polls is not excluded.
analysis_guidance.rtt_age: Initial RTT age is unknown. `CountRtt` changes only bound an update between observations; retain the last observed change interval, not an invented actual RTT sample timestamp.
analysis_guidance.reader_time: Read completion gaps include periods when `curl` emits no diagnostics; they are not pure reader scheduling delays. `curl` trace wall-clock values and reader monotonic observation times are distinct. Read/parse CPU, queue high-water and drops describe instrumentation cost.
analysis_guidance.native_controls: Each control has its own 5- or 15-second Job Object, inside the 90-second native-preflight umbrella. Both 16 MiB local H2 controls use the same 2-second output-reader pause; one disables tracing to retain a local CPU/timing baseline. They generate no archive traffic.
analysis_guidance.portable_checks: Linux `curl` 8.5 fixture checks do not validate the pinned Windows 8.23 trace format or Windows EStats/Job Object execution. Before archive trials, native gates require the trace forms produced by their fixture and zero recognized selected-line parse errors; later unrecognized forms remain a limitation.

evidence_limits.scope: These are JSONL stream limits, not an all-artifact cap. Result, configuration, source-hash and package-provenance JSON are additional evidence with bounded fields and observation counts.
evidence_limits.live_jsonl_formula: 8 live logical transfers times (2 MiB receiver samples plus 4 MiB H2 events)
evidence_limits.control_jsonl_formula: 2 runners times (8 `curl` controls times a conservative 4 MiB trace limit plus 3 receiver controls times a 2 MiB receiver limit). Several controls produce no trace events.
